title: The character--Picard sequence of a multiplicative isogeny
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups below are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $X^*(G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{F\text{-grp}}(G,\mathbf G_m)$ for the abelian group of characters, with addition given by multiplication of values, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Write $\operatorname{Pic}(G)$ for the abelian group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_G$-modules, with tensor product as addition; zero is the class of $\mathcal O_G$, and an invertible module is an $\mathcal O_G$-module locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_G$. A multiplicative isogeny is a homomorphism $f:G\to H$ for which $F[H]\to F[G]$ is faithfully flat and whose scheme-theoretic kernel is finite and diagonalizable. Faithfully flat means that extension of scalars is exact and detects zero modules. Finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra. Diagonalizable means isomorphic to $D(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finite abelian group $M$, where $F[M]$ has basis $e^m$, multiplication $e^me^n=e^{m+n}$, comultiplication $e^m\mapsto e^m\otimes e^m$, counit $e^m\mapsto1$ and antipode $e^m\mapsto e^{-m}$. Let $f:G_1\to G_0$ be a multiplicative isogeny between smooth connected groups, and put $N=\ker(f)$. There is an exact sequence of abelian groups $$0\longrightarrow X^*(G_0)\xrightarrow{f^*}X^*(G_1)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}_N}X^*(N)\xrightarrow{\delta}\operatorname{Pic}(G_0)\xrightarrow{f^*}\operatorname{Pic}(G_1)\longrightarrow0.$$ Here $f^*$ on characters is precomposition, $\mathrm{res}_N$ is restriction, and $f^*$ on Picard groups is pullback of invertible modules. The connecting map $\delta$ associates to a character the invertible module obtained by descent of the trivial line bundle along $f$, with the $N$-action given by that character (fix either sign convention). Exact means that the image of each arrow is the kernel of the next.

source.place: Proposition 18.18, sequence (129), printed p.391, specialized to finite multiplicative kernel; all connected groups are split over the algebraically closed F.

proof.text: Choose $B_0$ by [lem-sfb-borel-characteristic-picard-sequence] and put $B_1=f^{-1}B_0$. The comparison node makes $B_1$ Borel and identifies the two flag quotients with $Q=G_0/B_0$. Put $A_i=X^*(G_i)$, $C_i=X^*(B_i)$, $P=\operatorname{Pic}(Q)$, $D_i=\operatorname{Pic}(G_i)$. The characteristic node gives exact rows $0\to A_i\xrightarrow{j_i}C_i\xrightarrow{c_i}P\xrightarrow{p_i}D_i\to0$. Write $u=f_B^*:C_0\to C_1$, $v=f^*:A_0\to A_1$, $w=f^*:D_0\to D_1$ and $r:C_1\to X^*(N)$. The comparison node says $u$ is injective, $r$ is surjective and $\ker r=\operatorname{im}u$.

source.place: Proposition 18.18, proof and diagram, printed p.391; Theorem 18.15 and section 18.f, pp.390,395-396.

proof.text: These rows commute: $j_1v=uj_0$ is precomposition and $p_1=wp_0$ is composition of pullbacks. Also $c_1u=c_0$: pulling the contracted bundle for $\beta:B_0\to\mathbf G_m$ back along the flag isomorphism replaces its relation by $(g,z)b=(gb,\beta(f(b))^{-1}z)$, which is the contracted bundle for $u\beta$. Thus, for $\chi\in X^*(N)$ choose $\lambda\in C_1$ with $r\lambda=\chi$ and set $\Delta(\chi)=p_0c_1\lambda$. A different lift is $\lambda+u\beta$ and changes this by $p_0c_0\beta=0$. Lifting sums shows $\Delta$ is a homomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 18.18, proof and diagram, printed p.391; Theorem 18.15 and section 18.f, pp.390,395-396.

proof.text: This $\Delta$ is the stated descent map $\delta$, with the convention using inverse characters in the right-action formula. Indeed, on $G_1$ the pullback of the bundle representing $c_1\lambda$ has the frame $g\mapsto[g,1]$. Since $N\subseteq B_1$, the frame at $gn$ is $[gn,1]=[g,\lambda(n)]$. Consequently the descent relation along $G_1\to G_0$ is $(g,z)n=(gn,\chi(n)^{-1}z)$, exactly the relation defining $\delta(\chi)$. This is a scheme-theoretic calculation, valid on every $F$-algebra. The map $G_1\times N\to G_1\times_{G_0}G_1$ has inverse $(g,h)\mapsto(g,g^{-1}h)$; hence this is the full descent datum. The map $f$ is an fpqc cover: it is faithfully flat by hypothesis and quasi-compact because both groups are affine and of finite type. By [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] (1) and (3), pullback from quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{G_0}$-modules to descent data along the fpqc covering $\{f:G_1\to G_0\}$ is an equivalence and invertible descent data descend to invertible modules; full faithfulness identifies the descended line bundle $\delta(\chi)$ uniquely with $p_0c_1\lambda$, whose pullback carries the same descent datum.

source.place: Proposition 18.18, proof and diagram, printed p.391; Theorem 18.15 and section 18.f, pp.390,395-396.

proof.text: Injectivity of $v$ follows from $j_1v=uj_0$ and injectivity of $u,j_0$. If $a\in A_1$ restricts trivially to $N$, then $rj_1a=0$, so $j_1a=u\beta$ for $\beta\in C_0$. Now $c_0\beta=c_1j_1a=0$, so $\beta=j_0a_0$ for some $a_0\in A_0$; injectivity of $j_1$ gives $a=va_0$. Conversely $rj_1v=r uj_0=0$. This proves exactness through $A_1$.

source.place: Proposition 18.18, proof and diagram, printed p.391; Theorem 18.15 and section 18.f, pp.390,395-396.

proof.text: For $\chi=r\lambda$, if $\delta\chi=0$ then $p_0c_1\lambda=0$, hence $c_1\lambda=c_0\beta=c_1u\beta$ for some $\beta\in C_0$. Thus $\lambda-u\beta=j_1a$ for some $a\in A_1$, and $\chi=rj_1a$. Conversely $p_0c_1j_1a=0$. Therefore $\ker\delta$ is exactly the image of restriction from $A_1$. Also $w\delta(r\lambda)=p_1c_1\lambda=0$. If $d_0\in D_0$ has $wd_0=0$, lift it to $z\in P$ using surjectivity of $p_0$. Then $p_1z=0$, so $z=c_1\lambda$ and $d_0=\delta(r\lambda)$. Finally any $d_1\in D_1$ is $p_1z=wp_0z$ for some $z\in P$, proving surjectivity of $w$. All displayed maps are the specified restriction and pullback maps by their definitions above, so the claimed sequence is exact.

lean.note: The canonical-arrow helpers are part of this node as authorized by the stage-2 brief. Characters are existing group-object Hom types, written additively. The diagonalizable kernel is stated directly by an isomorphism with the existing Spec of a finite commutative group algebra, with its canonical Hopf structure; no second notions are introduced. The connecting homomorphism is existential with its complete character-equivariant frame characterization, not an arbitrary map or choice of an unspecified object.
